subject: Re: HIPAA / BAA eligibility and PHI deployment modes
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@medcare.org>, Jason Lee <jason.lee@medcare.org>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: HIPAA & BAA: deployment options and PHI boundary questions

Hi Sarah / Jason —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery on the HIPAA side and next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of what I heard from the call:
- MedCare will process limited PHI for the initial integration (patient identifiers + lab results, scheduling metadata).
- Procurement and security want a BAA in place for any production data flow.
- Preferred deployment modes: Dedicated or Private (on-prem/VPC) if available; question on whether hosted Redwood API can be acceptable with isolation controls.

Immediate asks / proposed next steps:
1) We can share a draft BAA and our SOC 2 Type II report for your review (attaching both). Please confirm whether MedCare has any non-standard BAA clauses to flag.
2) Please kick off the vendor security questionnaire and attach the MedCare questionnaire if you have it — happy to get that filled quickly.
3) I’ll loop in our lead infra engineer (Dev) to map the PHI boundary and confirm technically which deployment modes we can support for this workload.
4) Proposed times for a 30-min technical follow-up: Thu 3/12 10:00-10:30am PT or Fri 3/13 9:00-9:30am PT.

Attachments: Redwood_BAA_Draft_2026.docx, SOC2-Type2-2025.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@medcare.org>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jason Lee <jason.lee@medcare.org>, procurement@medcare.org
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 17:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HIPAA & BAA: deployment options and PHI boundary questions

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A couple clarifications from our side:
- PHI scope: initially we will send patient identifiers (name, DOB, MRN), visit dates, and structured lab results. We will not send raw images or psychotherapy notes.
- BAA: procurement requires a signed BAA before any production data is routed. For POC data we may be able to use synthetic or de-identified datasets but want the legal guardrails before prod.
- Deployment preference: dedicated or private is preferred. We need confirmation whether your hosted API (SaaS) can be included under the BAA if we restrict PHI in transit and require regional data residency (US-only) + customer-managed KMS.

I’ve attached our vendor security questionnaire (MedCare_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx) — please have your security/compliance lead fill out sections 2–5 and return. Procurement timeline: aiming to complete vendor review by 3/24.

Cc'ing procurement for visibility.

—Sarah
Sarah Nguyen
Director, IT Security
MedCare Health
sarah.nguyen@medcare.org

Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 08:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HIPAA & BAA: deployment options and PHI boundary questions

Sarah —

Appreciate the details and the questionnaire — I attached our draft BAA and the SOC 2 Type II report in my prior email but re-attaching for convenience. High-level answers to your items: 
- BAA: Redwood executes standard BAAs with customers for production PHI flows. We can surface any non-standard clauses early; please flag in the attached questionnaire or send markup.
- Hosted (SaaS) eligibility: our hosted API can be used for PHI only under specific configurations (US-only region, customer-managed KMS, strict network egress controls). For customers that require stronger isolation or to avoid shared-tenant risks, Dedicated or Private deployments are the recommended path and are fully supported under the BAA.
- Next steps: Dev will lead a technical mapping of PHI fields and confirm deployment recommendations; Rishi will coordinate contract/procurement questions and BAA redline flow.

Dev / Rishi — can you please 1) review the attached questionnaire from MedCare and 2) propose an internal tech mapping doc (we can share the output with MedCare) before the 3/24 procurement deadline? Also please confirm availability for the 30-min technical call — I proposed Thu 3/12 10:00am PT or Fri 3/13 9:00am PT.

Doc links: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/BAA/Redwood_BAA_Draft_2026.docx
DocuSign (BAA): https://docusign.com/Redwood/BAA/MD-2026-034

Thanks —
Marissa

On Wed, Mar 11, 2026 at 08:11, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Dev / Rishi — can you please 1) review the attached questionnaire from MedCare and 2) propose an internal tech mapping doc ...

Quick technical note from my side prior to the call: 
- PHI handling boundaries: Redwood can accept PHI in all deployment modes, but the controls differ:
  - Hosted (SaaS) — supported with customer-managed KMS, US-only region, strict network ACLs, and disabled cross-tenant caching. We recommend only low-volume PHI for SaaS during initial rollout.
  - Dedicated — strong isolation; recommended for predictable throughput and production PHI workloads. Included under standard BAA.
  - Private (VPC/on-prem) — full customer control over network and keys; available for customers requiring max isolation.
- For the questionnaire: I’ll start filling sections 2–5 and attach a technical mapping doc that outlines which fields we consider PHI, recommended redaction options, and example data flows.

I’m available for the technical sync Thu 3/12 10:00am PT — please send calendar invite.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Lead Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com

Attachment: technical-phimap-draft.docx (will share after internal review)
